items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: I got Eddie Condon's scrapbook... I noticed Eddie Condon again reading this book for the first time always talking about Mez... he hired people like I can think of first Edmund Hall and later his brother Herb Hall at his club

ctx.x: but I don't know who did he see in New York

do you remember oh everybody from Fats Waller of course was one of his big favorites too there's several pictures taken of him listening to Fats Waller I know and there's a picture I just got the other day I got Eddie Condon's scrapbook there's a picture of him sitting there with somebody was it like Duke Ellington or somebody I believe at some club listening to Mez and other people I don't know how they all got together that way but anyway Mez Mesro was one of his favorites he lived up in Harlem with Mez Mez was…

noticed it myself speaking about Eddie Condon did did did did Eddie Condon to your knowledge fulfill a kind of communal role for the musicians that outside of you know that set as a replacement for any of the New Orleans musicians did the New Orleans musicians associate with him at all

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: I never did really talk to Condon more in just a few maybe remarks here and there in my life he would hardly remember me if he'd seen me in late years he wouldn't have known my name

ctx.x: Yeah, Louie and Oliver and Bessie Smith just everybody that I sort of liked and including some of the Boogie Woogie pianists. Medlux Lewis was already in New York at that time came there in the fall of 38. No, that's right Medlux hadn't gotten to New York when it started on Jazzman. But I'd written an article on Boogie Woogie for Panacea's magazine which had come out oh, several months before we started on Jazzman and Ramsey had read that and liked the article so that's why he asked me to write an article on…
